en: *The Record of the Four Houses of Ciming* (with Preface) Chan Master Ciming Yuan (Successor of Chan Master Zhao) Chan Master Yangqi Hui (Successor of Chan Master Yuan) Chan Master Baiyun Yuan (Successor of Chan Master Hui) Chan Master Wuzu Faian (Successor of Chan Master Yuan)
Written by Zhang Zhong, Acting Court Gentleman for Ceremonial Rank, Newly Appointed Military Governor of Taizhou and Director of Educational Affairs.
The Linji school tradition is exceptionally flourishing throughout the world; indeed, its descendants all possess the soaring spirit of hawks and the piercing gaze of tigers.

Yet among them, only Ciming possessed a transcendent and peerless air that surpassed the common crowd. His vital energy swallowed the Buddhas and patriarchs, and beneath his mallet and whisk, he forged and tempered the ordinary.
The Sage’s functional mastery was transcendent; none of his contemporaries could surpass him. Thus, the Way of Linji flourished.
His successor, Yangqi, rode a three-legged donkey and trampled all under heaven.

Subsequently, Baiyun and Dongshan inherited the lineage, using the seal of the "No-Character" (*wuzi yin*) to stamp the faces of monks throughout the land. The Treasury of the True Dharma Eye was thus...
[This work] has perished at the hands of blind donkeys. Examining its grasp of the essential points, it is like uncovering the sun and moon;

yet later readers have been as if falling into a mist of illusions, only now finding this cart that points the way. Alas, Master Chan Master Bian of the Main Hall at Daochang Temple lamented that since the old woodblocks were lost, this record had no means of transmission.
Furthermore, those of us in this degenerate age merely dally with "fish eyes," taking them for the real pearl. How could this be?

Truly, those who understand the "night-shining jewel" (the luminous mind) are rare indeed. I have specially commissioned artisans to re-carve these blocks and titled this work *The Record of the Four Houses of Ciming*, hoping that the lineage of the orthodox and the supplementary traditions shall not fall into decline.

Now, the "Vajra Circle," the "Hawthorn Thorns," and the "Iron Sour Beans" are all brilliantly arrayed before you. If you wish to swallow and penetrate them without remaining within the realm of ordinary sentiment, it will not be otherwise;
I urge you to read this record. [End of] Shao... (Note: The final character "紹" (*shào*) appears to be a fragment of a name or a concluding mark, likely referring to the author or the scribe.)
Preface written on the first day of spring in the twenty-third year of the Xing period,
the Guiyou year. Recorded by the Śramaṇa Benyan of Zhidu Mountain Dinglin Chan Monastery,
the *Discourse Record of Chan Master Ciming as Abbot of Wuhui* (including the preface).
In the eighth generation of the Chan school, it reached the Great Master Mazu of Jiangxi, who divided the branches and established the lineages, causing the tradition to flourish throughout the land.
As the Master’s school expanded and students increased in number, the critique of "non-attainment" (feizhi) was lost, and the expedient mechanisms of skillful means (*upāya*) subsequently spread.
To sever heterodox paths, one must follow right view. Thus, Nanquan and Zhaozhou cut off the myriad streams, while Huangbo and Linji transcend the three periods of time.
To be a teacher is not easy; to find such a person is even more difficult. Only when the true milk meets its mate can there be harmony.
When Xinghua suddenly met Nanyuan, his spiritual sprouts flourished even more; when Fengxue encountered Shoushan, he finally attained realization.
Now, there is Zhao in Hedong and Yuan in Hunan. Zhao is like the jade resonating at Mount Shou, and Yuan is like the pearl produced in the Fen River.
These are peerless treasures for the age—how can their applications ever be exhausted? They are the true lamps for the final kalpa—their radiance cannot be fully distributed.
Alas! All people say that the sea is the king of the hundred valleys and that the dragon is the head of all things.

Yet they do not realize that the waters of the returning ditches flow beyond the Great Square, where their waves and billows cannot be fathomed; nor do they know that the Golden-Winged Bird devours them within its vast belly, where it could never manifest its transformations.
Now, upon examining the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan, I find it is just like this. I have therefore respectfully composed this preface. At the time of the Tianxing era.
Preface on the First Day of the Tenth Month in the Year Dingmao (the fifth year).
*The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chuyuan of Shishuang*.
The Record of the Master’s Initial Residence at Guangli Chan Monastery on Mount Nanyuan in Yuanzhou.
Compiled by the junior Dharma heir residing at Huangbo Mountain in Junzhou, who was granted the purple robe, Huainan.
The Master ascended the hall at Chongsheng Monastery and said: "The assembly has welcomed me to the front of the Dharma seat. The Monastic Official has finished reciting the proclamation."
He then ascended the seat and held up the incense, saying: "This one offering of incense is respectfully offered for the present Emperor.
We humbly pray that the dragon charts may remain forever firm and the jade leaves ever more fragrant. Again, he held up the incense and said:

"This one offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Provincial Governor, the Minister of Rites, and all the officials. May the star of fortune shine brightly upon you, and may the sacred grace endure long."
[The Master] ascends the seat. Again, holding up the incense, he says: "This one stick of incense is for the Chan Master Wude of the Taizi Chan Monastery in Fenzhou.
Now I ask you all: do you recognize Chan Master Wude? If you do not recognize him, you may watch freely as the incense smoke rises from the burner.
The Master then takes his seat. The Rector strikes the mallet and says: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should observe..."
Regarding the primary meaning, the Master said: "Does the great assembly understand? At Yiyang, Xiushui, Nanyue, and Shiqiao—if you do not understand, this mountain monk is deceiving you all.
Therefore, when Bodhidharma came from the West, he taught the "separate transmission outside the scriptures.
But tell me, what is it that is separately transmitted? It is the direct pointing to the human mind, so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha. Just as it is...
"Everyone here is a person pointed out by the Patriarchs; can you believe this? If you can believe it, you are fellow-students of the Patriarchs.
If you cannot believe it, you may be said to have brought about your own discouragement. This assembly today is no small matter;
surely the Minister of Works and all the officials have received the Buddha’s prediction from long ago, manifesting as kings and ministers."
"Establishing the Dharma Banner so that the Dharma may endure for a long time. Now tell me: how is the Dharma Banner established?
Is there anyone here with the spirit of an adept? Come forth and communicate this news! At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked:

"In the past, when the World-Honored One appeared in the world, Brahma King led the way in front and Śakra followed behind. Today, when the Master appears in the world, the Court Official stands before you."

The Master was presiding at the assembly. A student approached and requested, "I pray that the Master will preach the Dharma. The Master said, "Excellent. The student stepped forward and said, "If it is so, then I shall go forth with my bones ground to powder and my body shattered to pieces.
The Master said, "In the third month, wildflowers spread across the earth like brocade; in the ninth autumn, yellow leaves fall chaotically like gold.
The student said, "If it is so, then this single phrase of yours shall forever settle Nan-yuan. The Master said, "If one is a true knower of the sound."
There is no need for further hesitation. [A monk] asked: "The Langzhong has earnestly requested the Master to ascend the seat. As for the matter of the Supreme Vehicle (zōngchéng), what is it like?
The Master said: "There is a question and there is an answer. The monk stepped forward and said: "If that is so, then the waters of the sea will surge into waves and Mount Sumeru will leap about.
The Master said: "Though the great ocean is vast, the Dragon King does not find it secure. The monk said: "It is shattered into a hundred fragments. The Master—[remained silent].
[The Master] gave a shout. The monk responded with an assent. The Master said, "A staff does not strike a worthy man," and followed this by giving him a blow with his whisk.
He asked, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose lineage of the school do you inherit? The Master said, "A lion bites.

[The monk] stepped forward and said, "If so, then you are a true son of Fenyang. The Master said, "A mad dog chases after a clod of earth. He asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Tread upon it."
Zhuo was not angry. Jin asked, “What is it like to be one on the Way? The Master said, “A load on the chest and a burden on the back.
He asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “The whole family has been sent onto the boat. He asked, “What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, “In an acre of ground, there are three snakes and nine rats. The Master then said, “Cease your questioning for now.”
If one discusses this matter, how could it be like this? To speak much is to move further and further away from the Way. Therefore it is said:
"In the kingdom of Magadha, he already revealed his sharp edge; before the peak of Shaoshi, he entered the mud and the water. To reach this point, one must truly be such a person.
Originally, I intended to dwell among the mountains and wilds to hide my ineptitude and bide my time. Now, however, I have received the notification from the Prefectural Governor.
The Court Physician and the various officials have graciously condescended to request my presence, commanding me to continue the foundation laid by my predecessors.
However, as I am utterly incompetent in all matters, I am being suppressed and cannot stop myself; today, I shall become a laughingstock before these officials.
Is there anyone who can detect this? If they can indeed detect it, let us bear witness together. If not, then today this mountain monk—
"Failure. Standing for too long. Honorable official, I pray you take care of yourself.

When the Master first entered the monastery and ascended the seat, he said: "The authentic command of the Patriarchs—how could it be expressed through words? For the attendant to offer incense is already a matter of excessive concern.
For Śākyamuni to shut his room was already to involve prolixity. For the Layman to remain silent, on the other hand, resulted in saying too much. Why?"
Therefore, those who have left home and those who travel as mendicants ask people: "What is the matter of leaving home and traveling?
Is it wearing robes, eating food, walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; or is it extensive learning and great erudition, remaining silent and without speech?
If you understand it in such a way, it is like reaching out with a staff to strike at the moon. Since it is not understood in this way, then how [is it understood]?
"Is there anyone here who can distinguish between good and evil? If there is, come forward and testify before the assembly.
If not, those with doubts may ask questions. At that time, a monk asked: "The sound of the drum has just ceased and the great assembly has gathered like clouds.

The Patriarchal intent has come from the West; we pray that the Master will raise his shout. The Master said: "From where have you come? The monk stepped forward and said: "Fenyang’s single melody—the Master himself has sung it!"
"What is the situation at Nanyuan today? The Master said, "Do you see Nanyuan? [The monk] asked, "In the past, King Brahmā invited the Buddha for the sake of all living beings.
Today, the County Magistrate has arrived at the assembly; what auspicious signs are there? The Master said, "The rain of falling blossoms in the third month;
the bell at the fifth watch of a lingering dream. [The monk] further said, "The assembly has received your grace; this student prostrates. The Master said, "..."

The heavens are vast and the earth is vast. A question was asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Walking by day and sleeping at night. A question was asked:
"Where there are words and speech, these are all talk of worldly truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*). Is it not the place where a patch-robed monk (*bhikṣu*) practices when there is neither word nor speech?
We pray that you will grant us your instruction before this assembly of humans and devas. The Master said: "Grant this mountain monk a single thread of the Way, and I shall give it to you."
[The student] asked about the "Gardenia Tendril" (Jali-ge-teng). He continued, saying, "It is solely for the sake of its circulation.
The Master said, "A single sheet of white clouds spans the world; who among them is one who emerges? Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Water flows from a high source."
Question: What is the realm of Nanyuan? The Master said: "The waters of the Yellow River, winding nine times, emerge from Kunlun.
[The student] further asked: What is the person within the realm? The Master said: "The person following the current pays no heed; he turns his hand toward Fusang. Question:
What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Waves surging to the heavens within Lake Dongting."
The Master said: "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question? If so, come forward. Among all forms of offering, the offering of the Dharma is supreme.

Is there such a person here? If not, one must not force the matter by creating artificial occasions. However, I am no worthy vessel for this role, yet I have been unworthily ranked among the patriarchs.

On this day, how could I fail to receive the courtesy of the District Magistrate, who has deigned to lower his imperial mount and travel from afar to our mountain gate? Regarding the many... [text ends]
I am deeply moved by the Minister of Works, the lay patron (dānapati), and all the faithful who have gathered here.

Having long ago received the Buddha’s prophecy, you have now acted in this manner, uniting your hearts and exerting your strength to establish the banner of the Dharma. As it is said: "The Buddha-dharma is entrusted to kings, ministers, and powerful patrons."
Were it not for this person, the establishment [of this monastery] could not have been achieved.

May the elders and preceptors who are the masters of this mountain, as well as all the administrators of this monastery, past and present, together extend the boat of Prajñā and reach the shore of Bodhi. Now, I ask you all:
"Do you still recognize the shore? If you do recognize it, you will move with sovereign freedom throughout the heavens and the human realm.
If you do not recognize it, I have been thoroughly exposed by you all today. I have stood for a long time; take care."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The clouds have gathered and the mist has rolled away; the bright sun stands in the sky. Not falling into light or darkness, how can one communicate this?
At that time, a monk asked, "What is it to be among those of a different species? The Master said, "Long head, short legs.
The monk pressed further, "If so, then I thank you for the teacher's instruction. The Master said, "Half a sheet, entirely sealed. The monk said, "Going directly like this? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Ācārya, why are your nostrils in this mountain monk’s hands? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him. A monk asked, "I have long been a traveler on the road;
I beg the Master for a skillful means to point me toward the source. The Master said, "Eat when hungry and drink when thirsty.
The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then by following the Master I have attained accord with the principle of suchness (tathatā). Ten years of toil were merely to exhaust form and emptiness."
The Master said, "Three thousand [steps] by day; eight hundred [steps] by night. Question: "When one cannot find it though the mountains are deep, what then?

The Master said, "The mouth can bring about calamity. Question: "When there is surging in the east and submergence in the west, what then? The Master said, "Seek. Question: "... (The Master said, "Seek.")
"How is it when walking alone at night? The Master said, "Three bundles of thatch. "Question: How is it before a precious sword has emerged from its scabbard? The Master said, "Resonance.
The student followed up, "And after it has emerged from the scabbard? The Master let out a single sigh. "Question: How is it when seeking stillness within idleness?
The Master said, "A head pillowed upon a cloth bag. "Question: What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A lotus."
Huapengzu then held up his staff and said: "The Buddhas of the past, the Buddhas of the present, and the Buddhas of the future;
the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, the six patriarchs of the Tang land, and all the old monks of the world—these have all turned into Nan-yuan’s staff.
Where, you people, will you find a place to settle your body and establish your life? Look, look!"
"The staff has already passed through the skulls of all of you. Is there anyone here who can recognize its sensation?
If there is, come forth and leap before the assembly! If there is none, Nan-yuan has lost face today.
He gave a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat.
When the Master arrived at Chongsheng, the assembly requested him to ascend the seat. The Master then said: "This is the Dharma Hall of Chongsheng;
one must not speak of Buddhas or preach the Dharma here. Nevertheless, though this is so, official business does not admit even a needle, yet private matters allow for carriages and horses.
To speak thus is very much like carrying water to the riverhead to sell it. Is there anyone among the assembly who can examine this and see through it?
"Ma! Come forth and let us examine it. Is there anything? Is there anything? At that time, a monk asked: "The various dharmas have already been heard; today you expound them.
I pray the Master will directly point to the source. The Master said: "Heaven is not high, and earth is not far. The monk stepped forward and asked:

"In this way, the solitary peak rises above the myriad mountains; ten thousand miles away, a hundred flowers bloom anew. The Master said, "If you are not a guest casting the hook, your toil reaching the coastal shores is in vain.
A question was asked: "In the past at Vulture Peak, the half-seat was shared. What was the meaning behind the meeting of the two masters?
The Master said, "The wind from which it comes can be discerned. The student further said, "The assembly listens attentively. I, your disciple, shall now prostrate. The Master—
[The Master] said, "A person of spiritual acuity is hard to find. A questioner asked, "What is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas?
The Master said, "The silver moon first emerges from the sea; where is it not clearly revealed? The student further asked, "Do you permit this disciple to request further instruction?

The Master said, "The great ocean has no boundaries; it does not harbor those who dwell among the clouds and water. A questioner asked, "What is the Venerable Immovable One? The Master said, "Lift [the whisk]."
[The monk] did not respond. Jing said, "In that case, the entire assembly will knit their brows. The Master said, "What connection is there?
A monk asked, "How is it when traveling as a cloud upon the sea? The Master said, "Suffering."

The Master then said: "If you seek the principle within words, you bury the ancestral style. Even if you are thoroughly proficient in the meaning beneath the phrases, I dare say this person has not yet awakened.
Therefore it is said: 'The mountains are green and the waters are blue; sparrows chirp and crows caw; ten thousand streams share the same source.'"
The Ocean Cloud is naturally unique. The Buddhas of the future have mouths like lanterns; the Buddhas of the past dispense remedies according to the illness;
the Buddhas of the present follow along into pits and ditches. How do you speak the single phrase that does not fall into the categories of saint or ordinary person?
After a long silence, he said: "To add a point to an arrowhead. He then descended from his seat.
When the Master arrived at Yangshan, the assembly requested him to ascend the seat. The Master then said: "The precious mirror stands upon its pedestal;

the myriad phenomena naturally appear. The Great Sword is held in hand; killing and enlivening are applied as the occasion demands. Now tell me: is there anything that does not fall within its scope? If there is, bring forth a single phrase.
If there is none, those of you who are beginners or late learners, if you have doubts, please ask. At that time, a monk asked: "I know the Master..."
"Having lain long within the deep pool, what was the matter when Dayang ascended the hall? The Master said, "When the rain comes, the mountain colors darken;

when the clouds emerge, the cave is bright. The monk asked further, "I do not understand; I specifically request your instruction. The Master said, "Take up the winnowing basket and go pound grain elsewhere. The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "To play with the tide, one must be a man who plays with the tide."
A practitioner asked, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him;
he did not attain the path of Buddhahood. I do not understand the meaning of this. The Master said, "A case of total embarrassment (*mala-ra*).

The practitioner pressed further, "But what about the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū himself? The Master said, "An eighty-year-old man acting like a youth. The practitioner said, "I wish to study [this]."
The Master was at the age when one’s ears are attuned to all sounds. He requested the teacher to once again bestow upon him a skillful means. The teacher said, "The multitude rely on things.
The Master then said, "When people have not yet awakened, Great Master Mazu taught 'mind is Buddha. When people have not yet awakened, Panshan taught 'neither mind nor Buddha.'"
These are merely words of frivolous discourse. "Rolling the ball on the Snowy Ridge" is a performance that only deceives young children.
"Yunmen looking at the mirror" makes the bystanders laugh to death. "Shaoshi’s self-pity" is a great mistake. "Deshan’s staff upon entering the gate" was before he met a truly extraordinary person.
"Linji’s shout upon entering the gate" is far too flippant. "Huangmei’s presentation of a verse" shows that he had not yet forgotten self and others.
Furthermore, they speak of the patriarchs transmitting it from one to another, yet they slander one another in turn. To reach this point, one must truly be a person of substance;
thus it is said: "An eagle begets an eagle chick; a falcon begets a falcon. Even so, it is still just a tea jar from Gong County.
He then snapped his fingers once, descended from his seat, and ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the oil is exhausted and the lamp goes out? The Master said, "Raising a son who does not equal his father. [The monk] asked again.
[The monk asked: "Before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch, how was it? The Master said, "A mass of earth. [The monk] further asked, "After he saw him, how was it?
The Master said, "A mass of earth. [Another monk] asked, "What is the place where the Master enjoys himself? The Master said, "Fatigue. As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master struck him.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the Master’s family style? The Master said, "With a staff, he descends upon the dragon."
Hu Jin asked, "What if a superior person were suddenly to encounter you? The Master said, "A mindless one subdues ghosts and spirits.
He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "An Earl or Marquis rides a horse; a village elder walks with a staff."
A monk asked, "What is it like when one loses what came before and forgets what follows? The Master said, "No. The monk asked, "What is it like when one attains it once and attains it forever?
The Master said, "Carrying a stone, he threw himself into the river. The monk asked, "When a student wields the Mohe Mohe sword to take the Master's head, what then?
The Master said, "Take it and go. As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master struck him. The monk asked, "What is Nanquan?"
"Dog. The Master said, "Beak.
The Master then said, "All Buddhas and the Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi all emerge from this sutra.
He then held up his staff and said, "This is Nan-yuan’s staff; which one is that?"
"This is this sutra. After a long silence, he said, "The text below is extensive; it shall be entrusted to a future day. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Because a fellow traveler had come to visit him, he ascended the hall and said: "The scenery is cool and rustling; a fellow traveler visits in solitude.
Tea is brewed with water from the mountain peaks; incense is burned with firewood from within the caves. Be careful and heedful!"

Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and then said, "Even for one who is non-active and without affairs, there remains the difficulty of the golden chain. He gave a shout, struck his staff upon the ground, and descended from the seat.
On account of the falling snow, he ascended the hall and said: "The snow falls thick and wide; how can the water-clouds advance?
Tell me, how would you express the single phrase for retreating? Is there anyone who can say it? Come forward and try to speak.
Even if you could speak with such clarity and distinction, Nan-yuan would still not grant you his approval. But tell me, what excellence does Nan-yuan possess? At that time, there was one present...
A monk asked, “What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, “Bowing even more earnestly. The monk further asked, “What is the host within the guest?
The Master said, “The staff is always in hand. The monk further asked, “What is the guest within the host? The Master said:
Carrying his staff across his shoulder, he sweeps through the universe. A student asked, "What is the Master of Masters? The Master said, "A hand grasping a sword while holding a steamer.
A student asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A bamboo staff from Xiangxiang. A student asked, "How was it before Bodhidharma had come?
The Master said, "In Chang’an, every night, every house has its moon. The student followed up, "And after he came? The Master said—
[The Master] said: "In some places there is the music of the *sheng* and *ge*, in other places there is sorrow. A question was asked: "When the fires come from the four mountains, what then?
The Master said: "Things flourish along with people. A question was asked: "When not a single thing can be brought forth, what then? The Master said: "Hawthorn trees form a forest."
Question: "When the Buddhas and Patriarchs do not establish [anything], what is it like? The Master said: "Grass grows upon their mouths. Question:
"As for those who know there is something they cannot understand, how is it ultimately? The Master said: "A Bodhisattva’s face with a rākṣasa’s heart."
The Master then said: "All Buddhas emit radiance to assist in the realization of the meaning of the true nature (*dharmatā*).
Raising his staff, he said: "This is Nan-yuan’s staff; which one here is the meaning of the true nature? If you see it, you are turned by seeing and hearing.
If you do not see it, where is the eye of a traveling monk? He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? The Master said, "One cut, two pieces.
The monk pressed further, "What is the phrase for testing a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Hanshan and Shide. The monk pressed further, "What is the phrase for the true command being enacted?
The Master said, "A thousand come, ten thousand go. The monk pressed further, "What is the phrase for establishing heaven and earth? The Master said, "The heavens are high."
"The sea is vast. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "An old man develops an ailment. A monk asked, "What is it like when sitting side by side with the Master?
The Master said, "A thread passing through yellow leaves. A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary matter?
The Master said, "Try to say it and see. The monk hesitated; the Master struck him. A monk asked, "When the ancients sealed white paper, what was their meaning?"
The Master said: "The home is poor, but the road is rich. The Master then said:
"When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is fully contained within it. Within a single hair-tip, a lion appears;

within the tips of ten billion hairs, ten billion lions appear. Within ten billion hairs, a single lion appears. Whether there are a thousand heads or ten thousand heads, recognize them all as being one head."
He then held up his staff and said, "This is Nan-yuan’s staff. Which one is the 'one head'?
He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a single word that cuts off deliberation and forgets conditions; it cannot be obtained through clever speech—it requires only mind-to-mind transmission.
Furthermore, there is one more phrase, nothing surpassing direct bestowal. But tell me, what is this phrase of direct bestowal?
After a long silence, he struck a line with his staff, gave a shout, and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Three days of wind, five days of rain.
A monk asked, "What is it like when one brings nothing at all? The Master said, "Carrying Mount Sumeru upon one's head.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Not pierced by stones. A monk asked, "What is it like before the lotus flower has emerged from the water? The Master said:
The Master said, "It cannot be covered by the water. The student asked, "What is it like after emerging from the water? The Master said, "There is no hindrance to coming and going.

The student asked, "What is it like after the flowers bloom? The Master said, "Its fragrance spreads south and north. The student asked, "What is it like after the fruit forms? The Master said, "To feed the fish and the turtles."

The Master then held up his staff and said: "The Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and the lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges have all been swallowed at once by this staff of Nan-yuan.
The sentient beings therein neither perceive nor know it. Where, then, are the nostrils of you monks?
If you can understand this, you may carry your staff slung across your shoulder and gaze at the clouds and the sky. If you do not understand, [you remain] on the long rows of the assembly hall."
There is congee and rice on the bed. [The Master] lets out a shout, strikes the meditation staff, and descends from the seat.
*The Recorded Sayings of Nanyuan Shan* (End).
*The Recorded Sayings of the Master while Residing at Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou*.

The Master was at Xinghua when he opened the hall for formal instruction. The assembly welcomed him to the front of the Dharma seat. After the ritual master had finished reciting the proclamation and the petitions, the Master ascended the seat.

Having finished offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he took his place. The rector struck the gavel and declared: "O assembly of dragons and elephants, you should contemplate the primary principle."
The Master said: "O Great Assembly! Śākyamuni’s True Eye was entrusted solely to Kāśyapa on Vulture Peak; Bodhidharma’s True Dharma was first transmitted to Huike at Shaoshi.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Polishing a three-foot sword to transform those who are unjust—what is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Go well. The monk stepped forward and said, "Dot! The Master said, "Look at you. The monk clapped his hands once and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "Finished.
Another asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "There is no one who does not live up to their name."
The Master then said: "Coming up, one ascends step by step; going down, one is unimpeded throughout the body.
Therefore it is said: sometimes one strikes first and then sings; sometimes one sings first and then strikes; sometimes striking and singing occur simultaneously;
sometimes striking and singing do not occur simultaneously. Thus, when the King ascends the jeweled throne, the village elder breaks into song. Is there anyone here now who can sing?"
The singer says "Ma. After a long silence, he says: "Though the wooden man raises his hand, the stone woman does not lift her head.
He lets out a shout. Xuexia ascends the hall: "Last night, the heavens were covered in snow; the great earth was all at once bright and pure. This morning, there is no one in the courtyard;
do not say that this mountain monk has nothing to say."
Ascending the hall, he said: "All worthies and sages distinguish themselves by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). The mountain before is the 'supporting' mountain;
the mountain behind is the 'host' mountain. Which of these is the unconditioned dharma? After a long silence, he said: "The subsequent text is extensive;
it shall be entrusted to a future day. He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Dharma-body is formless; it manifests forms in response to things. Raising his staff, he said: "This is the staff. Which one is the Dharma-body?
Let us set aside this entanglement for a moment. It has already entered the nostrils of all of you in the Sangha hall and the Buddha hall.
The waters of the four great oceans are upon your heads, and the Dragon King of the Sea is there as well.
"Under your fingernails! Do you all perceive this? If you perceive it, then by day you travel three thousand *li* and by night eight hundred;
smoke rises from beneath your feet and fire blazes upon your heads. If you do not perceive it either, then when hungry you eat your rice, and when weary you sleep.
He struck the ground with his staff.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind blows briskly, the rain falls incessantly; the ruined halls and ancient shrines are all pierced through. My Peak stands solitary and lofty, piercing the azure heavens;
every Zen person who comes here finds it utterly distasteful. When the snow has not yet fallen, everyone says it is cold; how much more so when the snow is falling!"
To burn more incense only increases one's afflictions. "Go drink tea. Take care. [The Master] ascended the hall and said:
"The great sun rises and runs north and south; the night moon is full before the sky has dawned.
I do not ask about the phrase of hiding the body within the nostrils, but how will you all express the phrase of hiding the body beneath your own feet? Speak!"
"Is there a way to attain it? After a long silence, he said: "Familiar faces fill the world; how many can truly know one's heart? He gave a shout.
*The Recorded Sayings of Shishuang* (End).
*The Recorded Sayings of the Master while Residing at Fuyan Chan Monastery on Mount Nanyue*.
The Master entered the hall for the formal lecture and said: "The Dharma does not exist in isolation; it arises only by relying on conditions. He raised his staff and said:
"This here is the staff. Which one is the Dharma? Is there anyone who can speak to this? If you can speak to it—
From among the four modes of deportment, bring forth a phrase that accords with the Way. Is there one? Is there one? A monk asked, "The Master has ascended the Flower King Throne in four places;
what of the matter of returning to the West in a single sandal? The Master said, "Space is without obstruction; north and south may ascend as they will.
The monk further said, "Thank you, Honored One, for your response. The Master said, "Those who are idle are idle; those who are busy are busy."

Question: "The mountain is high with clouds clustering at its peak; the sea is vast as all streams flow into it. Without violating the phrase of the waves and ripples, I ask the Master to employ the 'biting the iron arrowhead' (niè zú) pivot.
The Master said: "At the top, it is insufficient. The monk pressed further: "If that is so, then the monkey cries atop the mountain peak and the wild geese gather at Hengyang.
The Master said: "Head and tail match one another. The monk let out a sigh. The Master then gave a shout. Question: "Just as one has left the rock..."
Shuang entered Fangzhang and proceeded directly to the Fuyan Dojo. Before the Prajna Terrace, he requested the Master to speak on the single phrase:

"Neither being nor non-being. The Master said, "Rarely have I encountered such a question. Shuang pressed further: "The bowl was cast down upon the peaks; ten thousand fathoms of cold in the vast sky."
The Master said, "Without passing through one matter, one does not grow in one wisdom.
The Master then asked, "Is there anyone else who has a question to ask? If so, come forward and create karmic conditions for the assembly.
Among all forms of offering, the offering of the Dharma is supreme. Therefore, when met with the high, he accords with the high; when met with the low, he accords with the low. Suddenly, if [all]..."
"What about when he does not come? He replied, "A total failure. He struck his staff and descended from the seat.

When the Master was presiding over the opening of the hall at Xinghua, after the monk-official had finished reciting the *xuanshu* (proclamation) and the Master had offered incense to pray for the Emperor, and the *weina* (chant master) had finished striking the gavel, the Master said:
"When a single speck of dust is raised, the entire earth is fully contained; within every single hair-tip..."
Each lion appears; from the tip of every one of its hundreds of millions of hairs, hundreds of millions of lions appear. [The Master] raises his staff and says:
"This is the staff of Fuyan. Which one here is the lion? Is there anyone who can say? If there is no one, [he continues].
A questioner asked with doubt: "In the past, the Brahma King invited the Buddha, and Śakra relied upon him; today, the imperial canopy descends upon this assembly.
Without falling into either of these two paths, I ask the Master to point it out. The Master said: "It has been thus from antiquity to the present. The questioner asked:
"I do not ask about the interlacing brocade and clustering flowers; what is one's original face? The Master said: "Once a word has left the mouth, even four horses cannot overtake it."
"A horse is difficult to overtake. Jìn said, "Brightly clear are the three periods; solitary is the single wheel of the moon. The Master said, "As for that solitary wheel—how is it?
Jìn said, "It would have been better to let it pass. The Master then gave a shout. He asked, "I have heard the Master say:"

When a single speck of dust is raised, the entire earth is fully encompassed. At the high peak of the Heavenly Pillar, how can one advance? The Master said, "I, this old monk, am inside the Venerable’s nostrils.
The student advanced and said, "A single phrase meets the point; today it is fully revealed. The Master said, "How much do the Venerable’s nostrils weigh?
The student said, "On the snow-strewn steps it is hard to stretch forth a hand; the frosty wind pierces the very bones. The Master then—
"Hai! The monk said, "To seek one peck of rice for another, one loses six months' worth of grain. The Master said, "One who recognizes their fault must surely reform it.
The Master then said, "Cease your questioning for a moment. In asking, there is neither horizontal nor vertical; in answering, how could there be any discrepancy?
Therefore, in the past, the King of the Western Heaven asked the Venerable Prajñātāra, 'What is the Buddha? He replied, 'Seeing one's own nature is the Buddha.'"
The King asked, "Does the Master perceive the nature? He replied, "I perceive the Buddha-nature. The King asked, "Where does this nature reside?
He replied, "The nature resides in its functioning. The King asked, "What is this functioning? I do not see it now. He replied, "It is functioning right now."
The King did not see it himself. The King asked, "Is it present within me? He replied, "If Your Majesty acts, there is nothing that is not it;
if Your Majesty does not act, its substance is difficult to perceive. The King asked, "When it is being used, in how many places does it manifest? He replied:
"When they appear, there shall be eight. The King said, "Tell me of these eight appearances.

Pratibhānu then spoke in verse: "In the womb it is called the body; in the world it is called a person. In the eye it is called seeing; in the ear it is called hearing. In the nose it discerns fragrance;
in the mouth it engages in discourse. In the hand it grasps and holds; in the foot it moves and runs. Thus it manifests everywhere."

This entire *sāhasra-lokadhātu* is gathered and contained within a single mote of dust. Those who recognize it know it as Buddha-nature; those who do not recognize it call it the vital spirit (*prāṇa*).
Upon hearing this verse, the King’s mind was immediately enlightened. Therefore it is said: there is no internal or external, and in the Dharma there is neither "this" nor "that."

It is simply because sentient beings, in their daily activities, remain unaware; they turn their backs on awakening and unite with the dust of sensory objects, drifting through birth and death, driven by greed, anger, and false views.
How much more so for one such as I, who from youth has lacked insight and whose affairs have been utterly frivolous?
To have been specially entrusted by the Prefectural Command to reside at this mountain temple is truly an overweening honor. Today, before these officials, I shall perform a scene of defeat.
[The text is] missing. Is there anyone among the assembly who can identify it? If not, this mountain monk has lost today. (He lets out a shout. He ascends the hall and says:
"The bowl is coarse and the ladle is fine; the spoons and chopsticks are short and long, not even a single pair. Sometimes he provides the offerings."
With whom did he discuss this? He sighed and laughed at Mañjuśrī and Maitreya.

“Take care! Having ascended the hall, he said: “The Dharma is fundamentally without words; it is through words that the Way is revealed. The Way is fundamentally without speech; it is by means of provisional speech that the Truth is clarified.
Therefore, when the Buddhas appear in the world, they employ skillful means in manifold ways. The entire Tripitaka is like administering medicine according to the illness. Three.
The three essentials of the profound are simply due to differences in the capacities of practitioners. The four selections and four patterns encompass all phenomena. You say:
"How do you express the single phrase 'the ocean receives the hundred rivers'? Is there anyone who can speak it?

Even if one could speak it with such clarity and distinction, they have not yet dreamed of the monk, the novice, or the probationer following in the footsteps [of the patriarchs]. Now tell me: what about the monk?
"What is the merit of the practice of perpetual celibacy? [The Master] lets out a shout. He ascends the hall and says:
"The sky has brightened and the drum has sounded; the holy assembly has gathered in full, with palms joined.
Is there anyone here now who does not join their palms? If there is, the Nirgrantha will rejoice; if there is none, Gautama will be provoked to anger. Take care!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "If the mind is without affairs, the myriad dharmas do not arise. When the will is cut off from the subtle and profound, how could even a speck of dust be established?
The one path that goes beyond—none of the thousand sages have transmitted it. Students exhaust their bodies, like monkeys grasping at reflections in water. I, this mountain monk, am not like this."
"The path leading upward is not realized by even a thousand sages; students weary their bodies like monkeys grasping at reflections. (He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was the intent behind the ancients' 'wall-facing'? The Master said, "He had years but no virtue.
A monk came forward, bowed, and as he rose, he gave a shout. The Master said, "Why do you do that? The monk shouted again. The Master said, "Blind! The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Wait until another time for those thirty blows; I shall give them to you then. The Master then continued:
"The autumn wind sweeps cool, stirring the wandering mind of the Chan practitioner; fallen leaves scatter in profusion, manifesting the auspicious scenery of the Way-man.
Wandering by the sea in the morning, lodging on the road at night—tell me, what is the single phrase regarding that road?"
“The Way. “If there is someone who can speak it, try bringing forward a single phrase. If there is none, Fuyan has lost face today.
He ascended the hall and said, “Every dharma is the original dharma; there is no dharma and no non-dharma.
Raising his staff, he said, “This is Fuyan’s staff. Which one is the original dharma? After a long silence, he said, “As long as there is a path by which to ascend...”
Even higher than those who practice as humans. He ascended the hall and said: "Clouds shroud the mountain colors; rain sprinkles the vast sky. Though the sun and moon rise, travelers do not see them.
Setting aside this entanglement for a moment, tell me: how would you express the single phrase "mud and water are not distinguished"? Is there anyone [who can]?
"Can you speak? Bring forth a single phrase from within your nostrils. If you have none, let the pillar serve as witness. [He lets out a shout. Entering the hall, he said:
"A hundred thousand wondrous gates all return to the single square inch of the mind; the virtues of the sands of the Ganges are all contained within the source of the heart. No [further words].
The three realms can be transcended; there is no bodhi to be sought. Humans and non-humans are equal in their essential nature and characteristics.
Since this is so, why did Nanda strike the imperial bell? After a long silence, he said: "The Persian’s nostrils are longer and longer still."
Ascending the hall, he said: "As for this matter, you have already attained it; there is nothing lacking. It is no different from the Buddha;

there is no other dharma. After a long silence, he said: "O worthy ones, have you not yet had a sudden flash of realization? The ancients, for no reason, bought it at a high price and sold it at a low price."
The Record of Sayings from Fuyan Chan Monastery on Mount Nanyue (End).

The Master entered the hall and ascended the seat. He said: "Dharma has no fixed form; it accords with conditions as its source. The layered peaks have just been cast aside; the great city..."

He was also called Elder Xinghua, who "opened a new shop in an old storefront. Yet few realize that whether in motion or stillness, in going or coming, there is no difference in principle.
Since the old shop has been opened, surely there must be buying and selling. Is there anyone here who knows the price? Come forth and speak before the assembly!
Consider this. A monk asked, "I have heard your words: 'The layered peaks are just cast off; the heavy city is newly reached. What is the Immovable Honored One?
The Master said, "In the morning one is an ordinary person; by evening one is a sage. The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then the great assembly will have someone to rely upon.
The Master said, "To sing the song, one must be a man from the imperial capital. The monk then gave a shout, and the Master struck him. [Another] asked, "In the morning one is an ordinary person..."

In the evening, the Master did not ask [the usual questions]. [The monk asked: "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'? The Master said, "Shenhui once wrote the inscription for the stele of Pujie.
[The monk] further asked, "What is 'taking away the environment but not taking away the person'? The Master said, "One must believe that there is another heaven within the jar.
[The monk] further asked, "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said, "The Son of Heaven within the realm; the General beyond the frontier."
Junjin asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are not taken away? The Master said, "The bright moon and clear wind come and go as they please.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "His face is like the full moon; his eyes are like lotuses. In heaven and on earth, all pay him reverence.
The Master then struck the meditation seat once with his staff and said, "Do you all understand? No?"

Upon seeing the Way, one forgets all that was known in a single blow; there is no further need for cultivation or maintenance. Those who have attained the Way in all quarters all say this is the "highest of high capacities.
When Xiangyan realized it in this way, he clearly awakened to the Buddha-dhyāna (Rulai Chan), but as for the Patriarch’s Chan (Zuoshi Chan), he had not even dreamed of it.
Now tell me, what excellence does the Patriarch possess? If you try to grasp its principle through words, you will mislead future generations. Directly—!
To try to take responsibility under a blow of the staff is to bring shame upon the ancient sages. The myriad dharmas are fundamentally at ease;

it is only people who create their own clamor. Therefore, when this mountain monk dwells at Fuyan, I see only the realm of Fuyan: rising late and sleeping early, sometimes clouds arise from the azure peaks.
The moon sets over the cold pond; the kalaviṅka bird flies and sings before the Prajñā Terrace. The *śāla* flowers scatter their fragrance beside Mount Zhurong.
Grasping a lean staff, he sits upon a flat rock and occasionally discusses the profound and subtle with the monks from the Five Lakes.

With his head covered in ash and face smeared with dust, he dwells at Xinghua, manifesting only the house style of Xinghua. Welcoming and seeing off guests, his gate connects to the city, where carriages and horses pass.

Crowds thronged together. Fishermen’s songs resounded through Xiangxiang; monkeys howled at the foot of Mount Yue. The sounds of strings, flutes, and folk ballads entered one's ears from time to time.

Furthermore, one would daily discuss Chan and the Way with eminent figures from all quarters of the world, until years and months were entirely forgotten. Now tell me: is this dwelling in the deep mountains, or residing within the city walls?
"Is there still superiority or inferiority? Try to say something. After a long silence, he said: "Wherever one is, that is Maitreya; where there is no gate, there is no Sudhana.

On the day the Master opened the hall, the assembly welcomed him before the Dharma seat. After the Monastic Official had finished reciting the preface, the Master took up the incense and offered a vow.

The ritual for the venerable ones concluded; they then took their seats. The *vinaya-dhara* struck the gavel and said: "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary meaning (*paramārtha*).
The Master then asked: "Do you understand? Formerly, the Great Being Mañjuśrī, before an assembly of one hundred thousand people at the Vulture Peak gathering..."
Taking the final blow as the sentence of the primary meaning, today the Head of the Assembly has reversed this command.
Tell me, is it the same as before, or is it different? If you can decide this, there is no need to raise an eyebrow;

if you have not yet clarified it, ask your questions with doubt. A monk asked: "The Prefectural Lord has issued a respectful and earnest invitation; the Dharma carriage crosses the Xiang River. Before the Peak of Throwing the Alms Bowl..."
[The Master] said, "Please ask the Master to cite it for you to examine. The Master said, "The wind does not come, so the tree does not move.

[The student] stepped forward and said, "If one suddenly encounters a master of the Way who cites it in this manner, will it still be appropriate at that moment? The Master then gave a shout. [The student] said, "This is enough to make one’s breath catch in one's throat.
The Master said, "In thirty years’ time, I shall give you twenty blows. [A student] asked, "When the thunderous voice resounds and the clergy and laity gather before the assembly, toward—"
The monk requested the Master to proclaim the Supreme Vehicle (Zongcheng). The Master said, "The waters of the Xiang River flow toward the east.

The monk asked, "The Supreme Vehicle has already been pointed out by the Master; with what first shall one benefit sentient beings? The Master then gave a shout. The monk said, "Blind! The Master said, "Precisely so."

The monk clapped his hands. The Master struck him. The monk asked, "In the past, when the World-Honored One held up a flower and Kāśyapa smiled, today as Xinghua opens the hall, with what will you instruct your disciples?
The Master said, "There is a question and there is an answer. The monk stepped forward and said, "Hanshan winks and Shide raises an eyebrow—it is already gone!
The Master said, "If you do not see the wild geese in the clouds, how can you know the cold of the desert sands? The monk stepped forward and said:
Entering the water, he saw a tall man. The Master said, "It would be better to pay him homage. The Master then continued, "Let us cease this exchange of words for a moment.
Questions are inexhaustible, and answers are endless. Therefore, in the past, when the World-Honored One ascended the seat at the assembly on Vulture Peak..."
The various great bodhisattvas each questioned according to their doubts; even those who were without doubt did so for the sake of resolving the uncertainties of the assembly.
How much more so today, in this single gathering—is this not a moment of great urgency? Therefore, the Buddha-dharma was entrusted to kings, ministers, and their descendants down to the present day.
Thus, we have incurred this honor and disgrace; we are deeply moved by the presence here of the honored officials of the entire prefecture and the venerable elders of all the monasteries.
The donors of this marketplace have witnessed this Dharma assembly; how could we not feel boundless joy? Now tell me:
all those many words and phrases just now were merely talk of worldly convention. Suppose someone were to ask now, "What is the principle of the Buddha-dharma?
How would you answer him? After a long silence, he let out a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In the kingdom of Magadha, there was no leakage of water; before the Peak of Shaoshi, this edict was personally enacted.
What is this edict? Is there anyone who can speak it? Bring forth a single phrase that blends mud and water."
"Is there anyone? After a long silence, he said: "The traveler, hearing it for the first time, finds his travel-sleeve damp; the lady, as soon as she sings it, lowers her azure brows.
With a shout, he ascended the hall and said: "One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function proceed simultaneously. To understand the meaning within this, look at noonday."
It was the third watch. He then gave a shout and said: "Tell me, is this the guest or the host? Is there anyone who can distinguish between them?
If you can distinguish them, you will walk three thousand miles in the morning and eight hundred in the evening. If you cannot, Xinghua has lost ground today."
Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation seat once with his staff and said: "A single leaf falls; it is autumn throughout the world.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I do not ask you about preaching the Buddha or preaching the Dharma. Not even an inch of grass grows—bring me a single phrase!"
After a long silence, he let out a shout, struck his staff upon the ground, and ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is the pivotal point of the upward path? The Master said, "Looking up at the sky.

The monk pressed further, "The green mountains hide the white clouds; travelers have never reached them. The Master said, "The Southern Dipper faces the Northern Pole. The monk bowed, and the Master [departed].
[The Master] struck him immediately. He asked, "When the One Vehicle of the School is proclaimed, the Three Baskets are cut off from expression;
when the Patriarchal Command is put into practice, the ten directions are brought to a halt. What is Xinghua’s core? The Master said, "I, this old monk, have suffered a total defeat.

The student advanced and said, "One person may pass on a falsehood, but ten thousand people pass on the truth. The Master said, "There is something in it. The student said, "Thirty years from now, this story will be great..."
[The monk] stepped forward. The Master then shouted. The monk said, "Finished. The Master then struck him. He then said: "The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs:
one seal seals the sky, one seal seals the water, and one seal seals the mud. Is there anyone present now who cannot be sealed? If there were, [he would strike them].
"Come forth! Speak a single phrase from beneath your heels. Even if you could speak with such bold clarity, first of all, you must not pass through the gate of a patch-robed monk.
Now tell me, what excellence does this patch-robed monk possess?
After a long silence, he said: "The three-inch blade of the king of men; the whole earth is filled with swords and spears. With a shout, he struck.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When a single speck of dust is raised, the entire earth is fully contained. He picked up his staff, struck the meditation seat once, and said:
"Ten billion Mount Sumerus, ten billion suns and moons, lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—all crumble like tiles and melt like ice.
He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To speak of Buddhas and Ancestors is to mix mud with water; to point upward or downward is for patch-robed monks to tear their straw sandals.
None of these apply here. To bind oneself when there is no rope—tell me, how would you express the single phrase of absolute liberation?
Is there anyone who can say it? Try bringing forth a phrase for this assembly in reverse. Is there anyone? Is there anyone? After a long silence, he said:
"Adding more mud on top of a grave. [The Master] gave a shout. He ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "I have heard it said in the teachings: 'Stop, stop! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and inconceivable. What is this inconceivable Dharma?
The Master said, "Today, this mountain monk has failed. The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then as for those days of old..."

"Five thousand [monks] with overweening pride—this morning, the great assembly has had their doubts stilled. The Master said, "By this single question, they were brought straight to a state where ice melts and walls crumble.
The student asked, "It is the student’s fault. The Master said, "One who recognizes a fault must surely reform it.
A question was asked: "When the lion lets out a single roar, heaven and earth turn dark. Where do the incense pillar and the lantern find a place to settle and establish their lives? The Master said:

The Master asked, "What principle do you perceive? The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. He then said: "There is a thing prior to heaven and earth; Formless, it is fundamentally still and vast.
It can act as the lord of the myriad phenomena, Yet does not wither along with the four seasons. He raised his staff and said, "This is Xing [the Patriarch]."

He transformed his staff into a walking stick. After a long silence, he asked, "Which one is the Lord of the Myriad Phenomena? He then said, "If you see that all forms are not form, then you see the Tathāgata.
With a shout, he struck once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the leaves fall, one knows autumn; when one returns to the root, one finds the ground. But tell me, what season is it now?
He let out a shout.

one plants green pines along the path. The Master said, "Were it not for this festival day, such an occasion would truly be difficult to encounter on other days.
The Commandant again sent the young attendant to say, "If that is so, then you shall meet with the Venerable One. The Master said, "From head to toe."
The Commandant then invited him to meet. As soon as they were seated, he asked, "I have heard that there is a golden-haired lion in Xihé;
is this true? The Master said, "Commandant, from where did you receive this news? The Commandant then gave a shout. The Master said:

After several days, the Master took his leave. The Commandant asked, "What is that one phrase for when you depart? The Master replied, "Take good care of yourself."
The Commandant said, "If that is so, then it is no different from other regions. The Master asked, "What is your understanding, Commandant?
The Commandant said, "I grant you twenty blows. The Master said, "Solely for the sake of its circulation. The Commandant then gave a shout and clapped his hands once.
