During their conversation, the Palace Secretary asked, "We face each other yet do not know one another; from a thousand miles away, we share the same wind. The Master replied, "I have come at the invitation of the Monastery.
The Palace Secretary said, "That is truly a deceptive word. The Master said, "I left Tangming last month. The Palace Secretary [laughed].
The Official said, "I have just now regretfully ventured to ask a question. The Master said, "An artist. The Official then shouted. The Master said, "Precisely so. The Official shouted again.
The Master drew a line in the air with his hand. The Official stuck out his tongue and said, "A dragon-elephant! The Master said, "..."
"What words are these? The Chancellor called for the guest master to prepare fine tea, as if saying, "It turns out you are one of our own.
The Master said, "This too is unnecessary. After the tea was finished, the Chancellor asked again, "What is the phrase by which Yuan Zuo-se benefits others?"
The Master said, "It is essential. The Secretariat Drafter said, "In that case, it is like a long-skirted bride running through the mud.
The Master said, "Who could equal you, Secretariat Drafter? The Drafter said, "An adept, an adept! The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows.
The Drafter clapped his knee and said, "What kind of place is this? The Master clapped his hands and said, "You cannot let him go either. The Drafter—
He laughed heartily. He asked again, "Do you remember the circumstances of Master Tangming’s initial awakening?
The Master replied, "I have also seen the Master cite this. The Secretary said, "Please do not withhold your compassion.
The Master then said, "I recall the Master citing it: A monk asked Master Nian, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Nian..."
The Master said, "On the outskirts of the City of King Chu, the River Ru flows eastward.
The Inner Secretary asked, "As for 'On the outskirts of the City of King Chu, the River Ru flows eastward,' what is the underlying meaning? The Master said, "A lantern hanging over the water.
The Inner Secretary said, "If that is so, then you have failed the ancients. The Master said, "If you, Inner Secretary, have doubts, seek another teacher. The Inner Secretary said, "Three-legged..."
The frog leaps into the sky. The Master said, "Leap as you please. The Secretary laughed heartily. After staying for ten days, the Master took his leave.
The Secretary said, "I have a turning phrase that I wish to entrust to you, Venerable One, to deliver to Tangming. Will you do so?
The Master replied, "The bright moon shines upon the traveler at night. The Secretary said, "But that does not quite fit. The Master—

The Official said, "In the deepening night it may still be bearable; it is only after midday that it begins to trouble people. The Inner Secretary asked, "Why has the Vajra [statue] in front of Kaibō-ji Temple been sweating lately?
The Master said, "I know. The Inner Secretary said, "As you are about to depart, Senior Monk, do you have no word for us?
The Master said, "The layered mountain passes and roads. The Inner Secretary said, "If that is so, then I shall follow you, Senior Monk."
The Master let out a single sigh. The Neihan said, "A true lion cub, letting out a great lion's roar.
The Master said, "Letting go and then supporting back up. The Neihan said, "Just now I tripped and fell, and then I was helped up by my servant boy.
The Master said, "When will there ever be an end to this? The Neihan laughed loudly. This is an examination and discernment.
The senior monk Ming from Xingjiao in Yinzhou arrived carrying a letter. Upon receiving the letter, the Master asked, "Did you come by the main road or the side path?
Ming said, "Try saying it yourself, Master," and then struck out a full prostration. The Master said, "Blind fellow, why are you acting so recklessly?
Ming let out a single sigh, and the Master struck him. He then asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied:
"Wrong," the Master said. "When it does not fall into the timing or the occasion, how do you speak? The monk said, "Wrong. The Master said, "Nanyuan was wrong;
you, Upādhyāya, were wrong. The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him. When the new Librarian arrived, the Master asked: "The ancients said..."
"Not seeing one another for three days—do not look upon me as you did before. Having been separated from the Abbot for an entire summer, how do you now regard one another?
Xinyue said, "It is no easy matter for the Master to maintain the abbacy. The Master said, "If that is so, then the Patriarch of the West has not transmitted the faith to the land of Tang;
Shaolin has needlessly established distinctions between kin and stranger. Xinyue said, "Why then does the Master [act] otherwise?"
"What do you say? The Master said, "Nanyuan has committed an offense. He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "The sun is already setting.
The Master said, "How do you speak a phrase that does not involve the journey? The monk said, "Seven times nine is sixty-three. The Master said, "Truly so.
The monk said, "This will kill me with suffocation! The Master then struck him. He asked another monk, "What is your age, Senior?"... [text ends]
"How many years old is it? The monk said, "Twenty-six. The Master said, "It is exactly the same age as my staff. The monk said, "Yes.
The Master asked, "Tell me, how many years old is my staff? The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him.
Seeing the monk approaching, the Master raised his staff and said, "It has already entered through your nostrils. The monk said, "Fortunately, you are a great Master, Master."
The Master said, "Understood. He asked a monk, "What is your name, Elder? The monk replied, "Haiman (Ocean-Full).
The Master said, "The ocean neither increases nor decreases; why then do you say it is full? The monk said, "Master, do not deceive Haiman.
The Master said, "Nanyuan commits a transgression. He questioned a newly arrived monk: "Since you are a guest in the gate of the Patriarchs, try to speak without touching the waves."
The monk said, "Venerable Sir, you are fortunately a great man. The Master held up his sitting cloth and said, "What about this?
The monk said, "A double case. The Master then struck him. The second monk said, "It is not that there is no striking by the Venerable Sir, but what can be done for me?
The Master said, "What excellence do you possess, Senior? The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. He then asked another monk, "This summer..."
"Where are you from? The monk said, "Xingjiao in Junzhou. The Master said, "Is Master Zhi well? The monk said, "He is well.
The Master said, "I grant you twenty blows. [The Master] asked a newly arrived monk, "Everyone has their own self;
which one is your own self, Venerable? The monk said, "My sitting cloth is made of seven-foot cloth. The Master said, "I regret bestowing it upon you."
Question: A monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Clouds pass over a thousand mountains, all green.

The Master said, "Why are you in such a hurry? The monk said, "The wild geese have flown away; the sound of the water is mournful. The Master then shouted. The monk also shouted. The Master struck him.
The monk also struck him. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow! By my fundamental right, I shall drive you out through the three gates!"

[The Master] said, "Outside! Thinking you are a newcomer, sit for a moment and drink some tea. He then asked the attendant, "I am not questioning you about the way of transforming within the marketplace;
tell me, what is the one phrase for entering the gate? The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Why do you shout so recklessly?"
The monk shouted again. The Master struck him. He asked the monk, "A guest in the gate of the Patriarchs, a member of the assembly at Jetavana.
The monk shouted. The Master said, "Why are you making such a mess? The monk drew a line with his sitting cloth before him. The Master said:
"Where does Nan-yuan's error lie? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him.
When the Master saw another monk coming, he raised his staff and said, "Why have you been swallowed by my staff? The monk said, "I dare not.
The Master said, "How can you be so reckless? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "Give me back the price for my straw sandals. He asked a monk, "The deep..."
"In these mountains there are no divergent paths. From where have you travelers come? The monk said, "From the prefectural city.

The Master said, "You have gone to offer incense at Nanyuan. The monk said, "It was unnecessary to say such a thing. The Master let out a single sigh and said, "This dullness is enough to trip up a man!
Sit for a moment and drink some tea. He then questioned a newly arrived monk: "Every person has nostrils. Which one is the elder’s nostril?"
The monk said, "I have recently left Mount Yang. The Master said, "Understood," gave a shout, and sent him out.
A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'Since the green grass has sprouted, I no longer descend the steps to walk. Where do travelers go? The monk said, "The journey through the clouds is quite far.
The Master said, "Nanyuan requests further instruction. The monk made a horizontal stroke with his hand in front of him. The Master said, "What words are these? The monk...
[The monk] remained silent. The Master struck him. He then asked another monk: "When meeting, one does not speak of worldly affairs; yet one must inquire about one's conduct.
How do you express the single phrase for 'the cold of winter'? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Nanyuan has lost face.
[He then] sat down and drank tea. He asked another monk: "How do you express the phrase for 'entering the gate'? The monk said, "There is no road leading upward."
The Master said, "Go well. The monk said, "There is no gate for entering the earth. The Master then gave a shout. The monk pushed the Master once and went out.
The Master called out, "Elder! Elder! The monk did not turn his head. The Master said, "Today Nan-yuan has failed.
He asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Yangqi. The Master said, "Where were you this summer?"
A monk said, "Xingjiao in Junzhou. The Master asked, "Does the monk Xingjiao have nostrils? The monk said, "He does. The Master then struck him.
He asked another monk, "When meeting, one does not hold it up; as soon as the intention is raised, one knows it exists.
What is this phrase of 'not holding it up'? The monk spread out both hands. The Master said, "Go to Nanyuan to prepare incense for an offering."
The monk said, "A transgression. The Master asked, "Where does the transgression lie? The monk pointed to his head. The Master said, "Too far.
The monk was speechless, and the Master struck him. When a special messenger from Jiufeng arrived bearing a letter, the Master said, "Xuansha sealed it in white paper;
why does Jiufeng speak so much? The messenger said, "In the chaotic peaks, the secluded birds sing. The Master said, "Not so."
While traveling on a mountain path, he encountered a man weeping at a fork in the road. The man’s messenger said, “It is noon, yet you strike the hour of dusk.
The Master then shouted, “If you wish to observe the person ahead, first observe the one who sent you! He then asked a monk, “A traveler must know that there is a matter of travel.”
"What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? A monk said, "I know. The Master said, "What is this thing you know?
The monk said, "The mountains are high and the waters are cold. The Master said, "Since you have come from afar, sit for a moment and drink some tea. The monk said, "Yes, yes.
The Master said, "Refusing to go while the weather is fine, you must wait until the rain drenches your head," and he struck him. He then asked another monk, "After three days..."
[The Master] said, "I have come to see you with my own eyes; what do you say to this now? The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master.
The Master said, "This dullard is enough to trip people up! The monk then shouted. The Master said, "What was that? The monk then struck him. The Master said, "You blind fellow!"
He then struck his sitting mat once. The monk said, "There is still something lacking. The Master said, "By my fundamental standard, you have been driven out beyond the three gates;
for now, sit and let me give you a cup of tea. He asked another monk, "You are a traveler who pierces clouds and crosses waters;

without touching the waves, try to speak. The monk said, "The tip of the Prefect’s brush has slipped off; it falls to the ground, and no one is there to pick it up. The Master said, "You are talking nonsense."
"Ma! The monk hesitated. The Master then shouted. The monk said, "The sun is at its zenith; I look up at the blue sky.
The Master made a stroke across the air with his hand and asked, "What about this? The monk said, "Finished. The Master then struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Beichan. The Master said, "How do you express that which does not involve the journey?
The monk said, "Shut your dog’s mouth! The Master said, "Where does my fault lie? The monk remained silent.
This is a double case. The Master gave a shout. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. He asked a newly arrived monk, "When meeting, one does not hold it forth;
when the intention is raised, one already knows it exists. How do you speak regarding this phrase of 'not holding it forth'? The monk said, "I am examining it. The Master said, "It is so.
The monk hesitated, and the Master shouted. The monk struck his sitting mat once. The Master said, "Blind fellow, you are making a mess of things!"
"What? [The Master] struck him and then had him drink tea. The Master raised the previous story again and asked.
The monk said, "I still have one more sitting mat. The Master said, "Does the Venerable One have another sitting mat? The monk said, "Yes."
The Master struck him directly. When they reached the Dharma Hall, the monk returned to the guest seat and refused to comply.

The Master went to the guest seat and bowed again, then asked the second senior monk, "Do you still remember the previous topic of inquiry? The monk said, "I do not remember. The Master said, "Note it down!
He then asked the first senior monk, "Do you remember? The monk said, "I am staring out from within a coffin. The Master said, "Speak!"

"I am staring out from within my coffin. As for you, Senior Monk, what do you say? The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him. Two Verses Sent to Li, the Prince Consort and Military Commissioner: 1. The Great Way is not far; it lies right before one's eyes. If you seek it elsewhere, you will wander in vain.

When the clouds part and the moon emerges, The ten directions are all clearly revealed. 2. The True Man has no fixed abode; He appears wherever conditions are ripe. If you wish to see his form, Look into the mirror of your own mind.
You dwell in the imperial capital; I reside in the forest thickets. Forest thickets and the imperial capital are like the Southern Star and the Northern Dipper.

As for the Northern Dipper and the Southern Star, who would dare point out their flaws? A thousand peaks fill the eyes; crows fly and hares run. Yet people still say that Hanshan and Fenggan were talkative.
I now respectfully bid farewell to the Duke of Longxi. Sitting alone in Vaiśālī, you roar like a lion;
the Golden Grain descends in form to adorn your followers, while you dwell in glory in the imperial capital, manifesting your noble counsel.
I know that this wondrous place where we have met is such that it causes the celestial fragrance to fill the roads.
Prince Li sends three verses to the Master:

The Sage has long been gone, and the world is terrified by the hosts of demons. How can one truly believe in the urgent task of "burning the hair on one's head"? Vimalakīrti remained silent in his empty room;
it was only Mañjuśrī who went to inquire after his illness.
The sun is warm and the hot winds blow for more than five months; by the waterside beneath the pines, I dwell in natural coolness.
When someone comes to inquire about Vairocana, I pluck mountain flowers with my hand and smile as I give them to him.
Strolling leisurely by the spring pond with my staff in hand, Forest birds and marsh gulls each fly their own way. The mountain temple is far away;
I long to inquire after its welfare. How shall we meet again before returning home?
The Master continued the rhyme;
among those who attained realization during the Image Age, many were such as these. Yet one does not know how they understood the meaning of "awakening.
When Kāśyapa struck the sounding-stone in the realm of the Flowing Sands, it startled Śāriputra, causing him to pass by in vain.

The Way lies in responding without distinction between the wise and the foolish; those who have attained it throughout antiquity and today rest at ease wherever they are. Fundamentally, the myriad dharmas are known without obstruction;
in every thing and at every point, there is nothing that is not the Way itself.
In the warmth of spring, everyone knows the orioles sing; The hundred flowers compete to bloom and flutter about in confusion.
Suddenly I think of the Elder of Vaiśālī in days of yore— Where have the Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas returned?
Furthermore, three verses sent from the Commandant:
"Encountering sights, one can align speech with silence; The Old Lu once awakened to the fluttering of the banner-wind.
One must know that for ten thousand ages he pities his lineage, And again sees the news from Vimalakīrti’s abode pass through."

Beyond the lake, the mountains and rivers share a karmic affinity with me; all this arises from your vast protection as you expound the true meaning. The secret phrases of Zhenyang are entrusted to those of like mind;
it is not like sitting for nine years at Shaolin.
Vimalakīrti kept his mouth shut—whom could he have known? Śrīgarbha’s eloquence bestowed much benefit.
I regret that, dwelling in the vast capital, we were unable to meet again and knit our brows in joy.
Because Zhang Jie presented the two Great Masters’ letter to the Master, the Master composed a reply.
At the end of the letter, he drew two feet and wrote the names of the two Great Masters beneath them, sending it to the Commandery Governor.
The Governor replied with a verse.
The black hair-tuft extends for over a thousand li; the golden coffin reveals the two footprints. Humans and devas can fathom neither; take care, O red-bearded barbarian!
The Commandant further composed a verse to send to the Master:
"Having lain ill for several weeks, whom else could you rely on? The four elements contend with one another—let them be as they may. The Great Being from the South has come to understand your state."
All! It would put the barbarian monk to shame and vex the child.

When the Master joins with Jin-sul (Golden Grain) to manifest his model, for whom is it? The cloud-like companions from the ten directions all follow him. When Gautama meets them, body and mind [are one].
Resting, he does not speak, yet still pities his eighty sons.
Two poems sent to the Commandant:

He manifests a thousand, ten thousand, even a hundred million bodies; His compassion, wisdom, and vows are inexhaustible. When among the laity, he conforms to the ways of the laity; When dwelling in the palace, he accords with the ways of the palace.
Everywhere there are great protectors; in every place they manifest spiritual powers. Cherish the good fortune of our school; many are able to establish the ancestral style.
Looking up at the single orb of the moon on the horizon, how many times has its clear light risen in the west?
The Great Being with disheveled hair asks Master Zhigong: "Mahāprajñāpāramitā."
The Commandant arrived at the end of the ceremony. At that time, he drew a single circle and presented it to the Master along with this verse:
"The world has no dependence; mountains and rivers offer no obstruction. The great ocean contains a mote of dust; Mount Sumeru holds a mustard seed. He then lifted up his head-wrap.
He untied his waist sash. When asked about life and death, he asked for the leather bag.
The Master then asked, "What is the Imperial Commissioner’s original Buddha-nature? The Commissioner replied, "Today is as hot as yesterday.
The Commissioner then asked the Master, "How would you express the single phrase for the moment of departure? The Master said, "Originally, there is no obstruction."
"Obstruction. It adapts to every place, whether square or round. The Grand Marshal said, "I am weary from coming late this evening; I will not answer any more questions.
The Master said, "Where there is no Buddha, manifest as a Buddha."
In praise of Lord Li, the Commandant, whose true nature is a phantom born of conditions.
Monk Yao’s marvelous brush captures him as a moon upon water in a cold pool—neither solid nor substantial. He came to manifest his transformation in the imperial capital;
he departed for other realms beneath the bright sun. The Lord Commandant of Longxi appeared as a peerless figure between the ages; he was fully accomplished in both civil and military arts.
The Buddha’s Dharma is now complete. I bow my head to Avalokiteśvara. Who among the Golden Grain [Bodhisattvas] knows all?

Onboard the boat heading for the capital, I compose this "Song of the Ever-flowing Yangtze": When shall I arrive at the Imperial City? Having obtained the favor of a cool breeze, I shall cease the use of oars and rudders.
The swordsman hides his sword beneath his fingers; how could he brandish it recklessly? The Way is difficult to distinguish when one departs from it; it is all because of a lack of equanimity.
Sent to Elder Jue of Langya.

The dream of this floating world is never-ending; how many times have we encountered such a human life? Knowing only the pleasures of cities and temples, one fails to realize that the mountain upon which one dwells is high.
All things have their own cycles of flourishing; for a hundred years, my heart has not been weary. Reflecting thus within heaven and earth, I am made to remember the Southern Office.
Sent to an old friend in Fenzhou: I often recall the days in Fenyang. In the Sandalwood Lion Grove, foxes and wolves have all vanished; wild deer alike are struck with alarm.
In the Dharma assembly there was no distinction between monk and layman; inquiring into the mind, there is neither ancient nor modern. Heaven and earth, I ask you: who dares to apply the needle?
Sent to an Elder in Fenzhou:
"Traveling through the south, north, east, and west; the Patriarchs of the east, west, south, and north. Shide asks Hanshan: 'At midnight, the sun is at its zenith.'"
The Assembly requested further instruction on the three decisions and three phrases, whereupon there was this verse regarding the first decision:
"The great earth and its mountains and rivers overflow; Vimalakīrti merely nods his head, and Mañjuśrī immediately becomes loquacious."
The second decision: When expanding one’s view of time and circumstance, how could speech and silence possibly interfere with one another? At midnight, the autumn moon. The third decision:
The mountains are distant and the road difficult to traverse; rowing a boat upon dry land, one picks out the sun and moon from within one’s own eyes.
The first phrase: Heaven and the other quarters are all at a loss; the various arguments of the *Cakravartin* are manifold and inverted.
Lofty and sublime, it has not yet reached the *nyagrodha* tree.

The second phrase: Linji and Deshan traverse the road and spread their influence; before even crossing over Silla, the staff is already brandished. For those who have attained realization, this is the path.
The middle line is a chaotic pointing and annotation.
The third line: Vimalakīrti manifested illness and Mañjuśrī departed; their dialogue was one silence that shook heaven and earth.
Even until this very day, it serves as a source of laughter.
The First of the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials:
How could the Buddhas of the three periods of time proclaim it? To bestow compassion while dreaming is to become frivolous;
to sit upright is yet to fall into the extreme of nihilism.
The second mystery: Even for a spiritually sharp monk, the eye is not yet clear; one who recognizes the spark of a flint or a flash of lightning is dull-witted.
Raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye is already crossing mountain passes.
The third mystery: The myriad phenomena are dense, and the universe is vast; clouds disperse into the empty void, and the mountains and peaks are still. Fallen petals drift away.
The waters fill the long river—this is the first essential.
How could one discuss the subtlety of the sages and worthies? To deliberate is to travel a long road; to lift one’s eyes is to fall into the seven perversions—this is the second essential.
Striking the wooden gong upon the mountain peak, those with spiritual powers come freely; those who rely on much learning cry out at the gate.
The third essential: to give rise to delusion is to invite laughter; within the palm one grasps heaven and earth. All myriad differences are illuminated as one.

This entire verse is offered to you, O Master of Profound Mystery: the staff and the shout must be applied according to the occasion. If you clearly understand the direct intent, the great sun will shine even at midnight.
The fifth position is "the central amidst the biased": at midnight, the black hen crows within the chamber; beneath the sea, a lamp is lit, its light illuminating the world;
upon a stone, flowers are planted, their branches and sprouts flourishing with vitality.
Correctness within partiality: as the sun sets behind the western mountains, one observes its strange reflection; the mirror-image clearly reveals the True Principle.
Cease searching for the moon in the well with knitted brows. Coming from the center:
the wooden horse gives birth to a child that fills the nine realms. Advancing or retreating, it moves freely along the bird-path; how could it be compared to a nest?
Dwelling within the confines of the realm, they arrive simultaneously at the center.
Each and every man fully maintains his spirit; as spearheads cross one another, their tips do not strike.
Expanding and unfolding in all directions, they remain inseparable.
Simultaneously reaching the center: before black and white, cease all making and doing. You must clearly realize that the pillar has not yet given birth to a child;
do not mistake deluded words for the path and wander therein.
This is the general verse on the five ranks.
Returning from the partial to the correct, the ultimate is profound and mysterious. When the correct departs and the partial arrives, principle and phenomena are complete.

One must know that the position of correctness is beyond words; its subtle signs belong vaguely to those with the karmic affinity. Reaching the state where both arise and depart, wondrous function is manifested; once one has reached this integration, why further pursue verbal explanations?
Appearing and disappearing, how could they encompass the entire world? Vast and unattached, the bird’s path is mysterious.
Yunmen’s Dharmakāya extends north, south, east, and west in myriads upon myriads; heaven and earth, above and below, are vast and boundless. Meeting and seeing one another, they laugh aloud:
pointing their fingers and looking up, the moon is half in the sky.
Question: "Since he is already at Sizhou, why does he appear in Yangzhou?
Dongshan said: "A gentleman loves wealth, but takes it by the right way.
Sizhou suddenly manifested in Yangzhou; the discourse-paths of the masters of the world are dense. A gentleman loves wealth, but takes it by the right way.
The Way. The nostrils of the Persian from the South Sea are coarse.
He asked, "What is the Dharma-body Buddha? Fengxue said, "The Mengjin Pass is not far;
most painful is lying down as a Tathāgata."

Only by following the current does one attain the wondrous; when meeting, it is difficult for the discerning to distinguish. As they leap away upon nearing the shore, the incense is burned without contention.

The two hall-heads simultaneously let out shouts, their arrow-like mechanisms of "pecking" and "poking" meeting point-blank. In that fleeting moment, guest and host were distinguished. The Master, pitying sentient beings, bestowed the black robes.
Ordinary. The waters of the Yellow River in the northern lands are thoroughly turbid.
Under the mountain of Zhulin, there is the bamboo-staff whip;
under the mountain of Zhulin, there is the bamboo-staff whip. There are myriads upon myriads of Chan practitioners from the north and south. Do not be surprised that when we meet, I do not dismount.
Horse! East and west, each has its own destiny.

Regarding Zhonggao’s request for instruction on the cypress in front of the hall—Zhaozhou’s "Cypress in Front of the Hall"—the whole world runs after Zen adepts. When raising a child, do not let him grow too large; once grown, he becomes a master thief.
The monk Huichao asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "You are Huichao. Huichao prostrated, approached, and joined his palms;
he pondered this for ten thousand miles in vain.
Two Verses on Lingyun’s Enlightenment Regarding Peach Blossoms In the third month, peach blossoms are fresh everywhere;
Lingyun saw them once and found no one more intimate. Everyone they meet says, "I shall retire from office";
Yet beneath the forest trees, not a single such person has ever been seen.
The wind-driven sails are hoisted; lifting the oars, one parts from the waves. For those seekers of Chan throughout the four seas, there is no need for further evasion or obscurity.
Yunmen said: "A steamed bun surpasses Buddhas and patriarchs—how can it be proclaimed?
A steamed bun for the midday meal is eaten to one's heart's content. In Hunan they spread their bowls; in Silla they eat.
Bite! The Great Eater of Persia seeks a ferryman.
Zhaozhou examines the old woman;
Zhaozhou exposes her. When the leaves fall, one should know autumn. How many Zen practitioners are there throughout the world? The Five Lakes.
The four seas are vast and boundless.
Nanquan smashed the rice-pot.
When Ganji prepared gruel and went to Nanquan, he requested that the Master recite the Buddha’s name before the assembly of monks. "Lilu the steward," he said, "is returning home."
Abandon it! At that time, the cauldrons and pots all leak through together.

Water flows from a high source—water flowing from a high source is truly marvelous! If the practitioner does not understand, their eyes will grow numb. If you have not yet clarified the mud and water, [you are lost].
Verse: The lantern and the pillar laugh heartily.
Commentary: Master Dushun’s Verse on the Dharmakāya:
“The ox of Huaizhou eats the grain; (The sands of the world) “The horse of Yizhou has a bloated belly; (The ants carry a bowl away) “One seeks a physician throughout the world. (A donkey’s head)
[The character for] "horse horn" (*ma-jiao*): apply moxibustion to the left thigh of a pig (drawing a tiger results in a wildcat).
The Cowherd’s Song:
The cowherd boy is truly happy; Barefoot and clad in a straw raincoat, he gathers his two horns together. Lying crosswise upon the ox, he sings toward the heavens.
Someone asked how it was that the ox had not yet become thirsty. He turned his face to gaze across the vast, level fields; let loose in all four directions, there was no need to restrain him.
Unconfined on any of the eight sides, he roamed at will. To bring him back, one need only pull at the end of the tether; the young calf is easily stroked and guided.
His strength is not yet sufficient to lift him up; for now, let him rest upon a small, level slope.
Fearing his four hooves might slip on the high peak, the sun has already risen high—cease grazing. Squeezing his nose firmly, young and old alike, they are all led at once into the pen to sleep.
Watching him as he wallows in the mud, falling this way and that, one laughs heartily—is it good or bad? Then, taking up a transverse flute, one plays to the wind.
A blast; it shakes the five lakes, the mountains, and the islands. Riding backward upon an ox, he sheds his coarse cloth robe. Those who know the Way need not seek it along the path.
If you ask where the cowherd dwells, he points east and west with his whip—there is not a single treasure to be found.
The song of the staff: its momentum and *ṣṭhāya* rhythms are beyond compare. Its curves resemble fierce dragons vying to emerge from the water. Held in the hand, it plays with heaven and earth;
moving against or with the grain, transverse or vertical, it rises again and again. The men of Wuyang cry out, "Chi! Chi! Chi! Gently twisting it, they cause him to look.
In the blink of an eyebrow, thousands upon thousands; directly beneath, one seizes it across ten thousand miles. Severing the roots of the vine, he picks up his cotton robe;
with a laugh, he strikes him right on the jaw.
Song of the Twelve Hours:

At the hour of Chou (1–3 a.m.), when the cock crows, one encounters people in dreams, all in a state of confusion and indistinctness. At the hour of Yin (3–5 a.m.), at dawn, having awakened, one plays with the spirit on the road.

At the hour of Mao (5–7 a.m.), as the sun rises, one sits within the shadow of its blazing and spreading light. At the hour of Chen (7–9 a.m.), during the time of eating, once full, one realizes that this very satiety is itself a cause of illness.

At the hour of Yuzhong (Yi): Buying and selling, weighing and measuring, entering the marketplace. At the hour of Rinnan (Wu): The myriad phenomena are clearly distinct, serving as objects of laughter. At the hour of Riyi (Wei):
Lord Zhang drinks wine while Lord Li is intoxicated. At the hour of Bu (Shen): Having awakened, one sits upright, yet remains in a state of drunkenness.
The sun sets at You (5–7 p.m.). The thatched hut and bamboo door are stiffly propped up. Twilight at Xu (7–9 p.m.). The sun has fallen behind the western mountains, yet the foxes have not emerged.
The hour of human settlement at Hai (9–11 p.m.). Mice gather in swarms before the bed. Midnight at Zi (11 p.m.–1 a.m.). A single bright moon, *sulu li*.
Praising the Dharma-eye and Dharma-lamp of the venerable masters of all quarters;
In dialogue and inquiry, they are as sharp as the meeting points of arrowheads; Shining through antiquity and soaring into the present, Yunyan and Dongshan;
The golden lock of the profound barrier, the five ranks of mutual interpenetration; The waters of the cave stream flow upstream.
Xuefeng and Xuansha—masters whose teachings are difficult to surpass; using blank paper as a message, they remain without flaw from ancient times to the present.
Miaoxi and Yangshan—light and dark, square and round; though possessing vast learning and broad understanding, their skillful words are difficult to proclaim.
The thirty-six postures—they apply expedient means according to the ailment. Shishuang and Daowu—father and son calling out to one another.
Three gates and five paths, widely guiding beginners; ruler and minister in harmony, how could they speak of existence or non-existence?
Mudu and Yunmen—lightning strikes and wind arises; the mud ox bellows, and the dark void reveals a ready-made koan.
They do not strike those who are already good; Linji and Deshan employ both staff and shout in unison.
Whether contrary or conforming, whether obscure or luminous—when the lion lets out a single roar, the hundred beasts vanish from sight.
(End of the Verses and Eulogies of Chan Master Ciming)
